purpose: Add nonduplicate boot/state evidence discovered after BOOT_ORDER_AND_STATE_HISTORY.json was created concurrently. This supplement is not a competing required-output authority and should be fused into the main history when safe.

evidence.claim: ASRS rollback and the microservice installer are first verified in accessible Git at the initial repository commit.
evidence.boundary: Initial repository commit is not an invention/creation date; content can predate import into Git.

evidence.interpretation: Historical recovery design recognized that integration rollback needs an explicit preimage spanning code/config/service state, not merely a restart command.
evidence.boundary: This is not an atomic whole-machine snapshot and does not prove coverage of all databases, process memory or external effects.

observed_mechanism.HARD: restore files/configs + restart affected services + clear caches
observed_mechanism.EMERGENCY: hard recovery + restart all critical services + safe-mode flag
observed_mechanism.postcondition: health verification contributes to rollback result

evidence.important_detail: Before restoring an existing file the implementation writes a .pre_rollback emergency backup, then restores from the baseline backup.
evidence.boundary: Recorded rollback success is implementation logic, not reproduced historical runtime success in this research step.

observed_mechanism: dream meta-watchdog declares ordering after dream watchdog
llm-guard declares ordering/want on llama3 GPU service
installer enables infrastructure, daemon, autonomous, watchdog/body and scheduled tiers
evidence.counterhypothesis: Tier labels and systemd After/Wants/Requires relationships do not establish application-level endpoint readiness or a single transactional boot barrier.
evidence.next_discriminator: Extract a versioned service dependency graph and compare declared ordering with observed boot/restart traces.

observed_mechanism: frank-soma-sleep.timer uses Persistent=true but is deliberately not enabled by default; Personal Mode activation is separate
aicore-fas.timer uses Persistent=true and is enabled by installer
aicore-llama3-restart.timer periodically invokes an RSS watchdog
evidence.interpretation: Scheduled-task definition, persistence/catch-up semantics and activation authority were separate concerns in the historical installer.
evidence.boundary: Timer firing does not establish task/model/training success.

evidence.observed_mechanism: Allowed service name is encoded into a restart request written via temporary-file then rename; the watchdog is expected to consume/execute the request.
evidence.interpretation: Request and effect are separate lifecycle stages even in the historical restart path.
evidence.boundary: Writing restart_request.json is not proof that systemd restarted the service or that the service became ready.

evidence.observed_history: Two broad path-systematization passes removed host-specific home/tmp/runtime/database assumptions; _bootstrap.py stabilizes source-root imports for CLI/systemd entrypoints.
evidence.interpretation: Boot and recovery correctness depended on coherent path authority, not only process dependency order.
evidence.boundary: Portable path resolution does not itself prove boot success.

evidence.observed_history: Voice/wallpaper services were removed; SOMA service/timer was added but activation kept conditional; later installer cleanup removed Ollama/AURA/legacy entity timers and moved entity scheduling toward room_dispatcher.
evidence.interpretation: A timeless flat service list would falsify the actual lineage; boot topology needs version identity.
evidence.boundary: Commit descriptions remain historical Git evidence unless exact diffs/runtime are separately verified.

evidence.observed_history: Bare except handlers were replaced because they catch SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt and can prevent clean shutdown.
evidence.interpretation: Shutdown/recovery semantics depend on exception boundaries as well as service-manager configuration.
evidence.boundary: Commit message claim; no independent historical runtime reproduction here.

cross_cutting_synthesis.reason: Historical state spans file/config backups, durable databases, systemd state, transient restart signals and process state; external effects are not covered by a service restart.
cross_cutting_synthesis.falsifier: Demonstrate an exact state-class inventory in which service restart alone deterministically reconstructs and verifies every required state class including external effect outcomes.

cross_cutting_synthesis.reason: The frozen installer relies heavily on After/Wants/Requires while many units share default.target; no readiness-barrier trace was observed in this step.
cross_cutting_synthesis.falsifier: Repository-bound repeated cold/restart traces prove each consumer waits on explicit provider readiness with no race-sensitive failures.

cross_cutting_synthesis.reason: ASRS already captured checksums/config/service state, but current EntityOS requires stronger provenance/generation/effect boundaries than the historical mechanism exposed.
cross_cutting_synthesis.falsifier: Show equivalent recovery correctness under stale/mismatched generation without explicit identity binding.

reuse: exact preimage capture before risky mutation
adapt: systemd dependency graph into explicit typed lifecycle/readiness contracts
ASRS baseline identity into current generation/provenance/effect-journal boundaries
do_not_promote: historical restart success into current runtime credit
timer/service presence into activation or outcome evidence
historical watchdog layering into current architecture without quiescence/restart-storm tests

next_exact_action: Fuse this delta into BOOT_ORDER_AND_STATE_HISTORY.json only after re-entering current main and preserving the concurrently authored timeline; then extract the versioned systemd/service dependency graph and persistence-lifetime classes without overwriting independent evidence.
